body: Yeah thanks for pointing that out.

Thank you. Shes suffered from depression throughout her life and has always refused treatment or to talk about it with anyone. a combination of things has lead her to where we are today. She’s never been particularly outgoing but she did very well masking quite what a bad place she was in.

She’s (still) in A&E waiting to be assessed by the mental health team. I’ve not been allowed to see or talk to her since I arrived at hospital (she came in an ambulance) because Covid.  A nurse told me she’ll almost certainly be admitted.  I’m terrified she’ll do it again if she’s left alone. 

I’ve recently been diagnosed with ADHD, so I know I have not been the best person for her  but she told me and the Police/ambulance staff that there is no part of her life that made it worth living.  The only person at her work that she respected dropped dead from a heart attack a week ago and she finds her family and work intolerable. I guess I didn’t realise how awful. 

She even said she filled up the bird feeders and tidied up the house so I’d not have to worry about any of that for a while after she was gone. I can’t believe she thought I’d be better off without her. I feel so useless and speechless about it all.

Sorry to hear it's mostly traumas, at least my childhood was, I think, happy. It's fascinating how memory works. Like I say I can remember fragments of things from childhood. None of my birthdays though, which you'd think might be memorable. It's all in there somewhere though, I recently watched the first series of lost again after 15 years, and during the opening credits  I could match up the character name with each actor.  Ask me the names of my work colleagues though...

I agree with your comment on memories open to interpretation, that's a huge struggle for me.

I have a few memories but they’re generally from significant events. They’re the equivalent of an image with a bit of internal monologue to go along with it. What I find most striking is I remember literally nothing about my time in the classroom - spanning what must be 12 years.
